profile.entities: Bajaj Electricals Ltd (Parent); No specific subsidiaries detailed
profile.subseg: Lighting Solutions (Professional & Consumer); Consumer Products (Fans, Kitchen Appliances, Coolers, Irons, Water Heaters); Wires & Switchgears
profile.themes: Channel Inventory Correction; BLDC Fan Gap; War-Driven Input Inflation; Strategic Shift to Sell-Through

deepdive.sec: Consumer Durables & Electricals / Energy Transition Infrastructure

bull_bear.body: Dividend: INR 3/share (150% of face value) recommended for FY26; Cash flow positive (INR 400 Cr operating cash flow in Q4); Focus on brand building and innovation spend in next 12 months.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delayed/patchy summer season impacting fans/coolers; War-geopolitical input cost inflation; Market share loss in Fans due to BLDC technology gap; Demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about Consumer Products struggles; Confident in Lighting trajectory; Emphasis on 'cultural change' and sustainable profitability over volume push.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly stated they will reinvest Lighting margin gains to accelerate growth rather than bottom-line expansion; Fan segment weakness specifically tied to lack of competitive BLDC offerings vs. traditional induction strength; Inventory correction in coolers still ongoing but deemed non-material for full year.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Lighting Solutions: 16% Q4 revenue growth, 8.7% Q4 EBIT margin, 8.5% annual EBIT margin. Consumer Products: Kitchen appliances +30% growth; Fans and Coolers negative due to delayed summer and high channel inventory; Irons/Water Heaters modest growth. Wires: New entry with strong market response.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input cost inflation and demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through | Competitors with lower pricing power | loser | Med | Bajaj's brand strength allows partial pass-through (3-10%), squeezing weaker players. |
| Gap in BLDC fan technology causing market share loss | Havells India; Crompton Greaves | beneficiary | High | Peers with stronger BLDC portfolios are capturing the growing energy-efficient fan segment where Bajaj is weak. |
| Channel inventory correction creating short-term pain | Bajaj Electricals Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Once inventory normalizes (expected by FY27), sell-through data should reflect healthier demand without channel stuffing distortions. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Lighting margins supported by premium mix; Consumer margins pressured by war-related inflation (partially passed via 3-10% price hikes) and inability to fully pass on costs due to demand uncertainty; Operating deleverage in Consumer vertical due to volume drop.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Intent to grow ahead of market (mid-single digit industry avg). Margin: Lighting EBIT likely stable as gains reinvested for growth; Consumer targetting industry avg 6-9% EBIT over medium term. Order Inflow: Strong in Wires/Switchgears. Capex: Substantial reduction in FY27/FY28 (<50% of past levels), focused on mould replacement and innovation.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Wires category launched in Feb FY26 seeing immediate robust orders; Professional and Consumer Lighting trade growing; No specific numeric order book value provided.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Wires category as new growth driver; Bridging BLDC fan technology gap to recover market share; Premiumization in Lighting; Expansion in Professional Lighting.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Bajaj Electricals delivered a modest Q4FY26 with Lighting Solutions hitting record margins (8.5% annual) while Consumer Products faced losses due to delayed summer and intentional channel de-stocking. The strategic pivot from volume-push to demand-led sell-through is progressing, with inventory normalization expected to drive a rebound in FY27, though fan market share erosion due to BLDC gaps remains a critical near-term headwind.
